newsitem.title: USA: NY trial of Venezuelan bankers nears close.
newsitem.headline: NY trial of Venezuelan bankers nears close.

text.p: The lawyer for a banker being tried with his son and grandson for defrauding Venezuelan depositors on Monday urged the New York jury to acquit his client because "they have not proved that he took a dollar".

Cuban-born Orlando Castro Llanes, his son Orlando Castro and grandson Jorge Castro Barredo are accused of illegally using deposits in a family-controlled bank, Banco Progreso International de Puerto Rico, to prop up financial institutions in Central and South America.
The case was tried in New York because prosecutors charged that the money in the alleged frauds was transferred through New York banks, including two multimillion dollar transfers.

In his closing arguments in the three-month trial, attorney Richard Sharpstein criticized Manhattan District Attorney Robert Morgenthau for prosecuting a case he claimed had nothing to do with New York banking.
"Nobody in New York is complaining, nobody in New York was ripped off ... They have not proved that he took a dollar, nothing," Sharpstein said.

The prosecution contends the three bankers misled Venezuelan depositors to believe the Puerto Rican bank was a safe off-shore bank subject to tight regulatory control, attracting deposits of more than $55 million. The bank folded in January 1995 with uninsured losses to depositors of more than $15 million.
Lawyers for the other two defendants will present their closing arguments on Tuesday.
The 12 jurors hearing the complicated financial case include a retired union member, two nurses, an actor and an unemployed parking attendant.

Morgenthau has acknowledged he took on the case at the request of Venezuelan Attorney General Jesus Petit da Costa. He claims that when a banking system goes bankrupt, it affects the whole banking system, including New York's.
"When a national government has lost $7 billion and the attorney general says to you, 'Will you help us?' you've got to respond 'Yes,' if you have jurisdiction and I think we did," Morgenthau said.
